1	# 2D Lighting & Occlusion
2	
3	> Authoring guidance: .claude/docs/templates/guidance/game-design-document-guide.md (load per-section as you author — do not read entirely).
4	
5	> **Status**: Designed
6	> **Author**: user + technical-artist, godot-shader-specialist, engine-programmer, creative-director (via /design-system, autonomous; orchestrated run 2026-10-26)
7	> **Last Updated**: 2026-10-27 (first formal design review; user rulings applied the same day)
8	> **Last Verified**: 2026-10-26 (statuses of dependent systems re-verified 2026-10-27)
9	> **Implements Pillar**: P1 The World Never Lies (primary — the drawn edge of every real light is the edge the simulation queries: hard cones end at `reach_px` ±1 px, soft pools end at `r_off` ±1 px (the latch-release radius, with the approach prompt `band_px` inside it, LO-7), occlusion is true occlusion with no vignette, fog or mask, and lamp brightness rides the Graph's closed consequence channel so no hallucination can change it); P3 The Web Watches (primary — emission is exposure: every running loop is a lantern drawn here, going dark is legible as light, and Attention's light-side tell is rendered as a gutter in the world, never as a meter). **Serves**: P4 Sanity Rewrites Reality (channel owner, not content owner: Lighting owns the one place a light-shaped lie may be drawn, a leaking overlay on a Lighting-owned layer, and guarantees the real light beneath it never moves); P2 Dread Before Chaos (the beacon sweep, the gutter and fault glows appearing on the Graph tick are the light channel of the 10–30 s tell, all inside the flash governor); P5 Deeper Is Richer, Loss Is Not Total (weakly: depth sets only the ambient-floor ordering, never reach or hue, so the ring ordering is not a difficulty dial)
10	> **Creative Director Review (CD-GDD-ALIGN)**: CONCERNS → REVISED 2026-10-26 (4 items applied)
11	> **Design Review (first formal /design-review, 2026-10-27)**: REVISED. 5 BLOCKING findings and the clear RECOMMENDED findings applied; every edited paragraph or row carries *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The creative contract this revision protects: **the drawn edge equals the prompt edge** (LO-7), at every tier, rung and pass. Items that needed a person's call were ruled by the user on 2026-10-27 (next line).
12	> **User rulings (design-review decisions, 2026-10-27)**: the user ruled "I agree with all of your recommendations on those decisions" and answered "yes to all" on the held list. Applied here as **user rulings**: D31 (the PD-1/PD-1b residual bounds are accepted as scoped MVP exceptions, Open Question 21), X2 (the docked pod's dock-room status glow is an ordinary lit fixture, LO-34), X9 (the flash counting unit ceil(N / 2) is ratified, LO-22), D24 (`BEAM_SPILL` shape row 11, LO-35), and the confirmations D20-D23 (Emitter State's four provisional rulings stand; darkness is never a sanity cost). Applied as **defaults confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20)**: D32 (Emitter State adopts `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS`; no Lighting exception), D33 (Open Questions 1-5 and 23 take their current defaults), D79/X10 (`reduce_flashing` defaults ON at first launch). **X14 closed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R12):** the reference machines are RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK and the build is a Godot 4.7.2 release export (`project.yaml` `qa.min_spec`); Lighting's performance figures are pending spike measurement on them (Open Question 28). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)* The 2026-10-26 CD-GDD-ALIGN approval predates these amendments. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
13	> **Re-review (2026-10-27)**: REVISED. The four BLOCKING findings are resolved (stand-in clamp withdrawn; the pool radius read from Emitter State's `r_lit_px` chain with the `r_off_px` publication agreed 2026-10-28; the darkening contract for characters, web, filaments and horrors under carrier B; the 24 px bound kept per delegated ruling R7, with `spine_corridor` owed by Derelict Authoring) and the clear RECOMMENDED findings applied; every edited paragraph or row carries *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Open Questions 31-36 are new. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
14	> **Cross-GDD fix pass (2026-10-28)**: `r_off_px` is now read from Emitter State's 17-field view (Lighting no longer runs the chain; Open Question 25 resolved), the `BEAM_SPILL` foot pool is read through `beam_spill(beam_id)` (LO-5, LO-35), AC-LO-28 now tests the hash-gap onsets of D.15, X14 is closed by R12 (RM-DESKTOP, RM-DECK; Open Question 28 keeps only the GPU sub-budget). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
15	> **Confirming-review fix pass (2026-10-28)**: LO-15's default texture layout is now the grown square (side `A`) for narrow, beacon and split, so the shipped default passes its own axial fit test and boot rule AC-LO-78 (G3/G4); D.2, D.3 and D.9-D.11 are restated at `D_tex` 5.22 / 5.95 (ESTIMATE until spike step 2); the dock status glow (`subkind` DOCK_STATUS) is exempt from L1, L2 and L3 as a system-switched status light (Attention AT-20, user ruling X2; G6). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, G3/G4; cross-GDD fix, G6)*
16	
17	## Summary
18	
19	2D Lighting & Occlusion draws every light in the game: the player's chest-mounted beam, ship lamps, the glow of running machinery, the alarm beacon, glowsticks and fault glows, with real shadows from walls and a hull that is never fully black. It decides nothing about the world. It draws the facts Emitter State publishes, so the edge the player sees is the edge the game acts on (a prompt appears exactly where the light visibly ends), and it is the single place a light-shaped hallucination may be drawn, always as a violet-leaking overlay that never changes the real light beneath it. Skip it for what a light means (Emitter State) or where walls are (Layout).
20	
21	**Terms.** `reach_px` is the simulation's fade-out distance. `r_off` is the radius a soft pool is drawn to (the latch-release radius) and `r_lit` is the radius at which an approaching subject first meets its prompt, a few px inside it. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A slot is one of six shadow-casting lights. A layer is one step of the modifier chain. A stand-in is the additive disc, drawn to the same edge as the light it replaces, that stands in for an over-budget light. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A decoy is an unlit hallucination overlay, never a light. The tell tier is Attention's published level, drawn as a gutter on lamps.
22	
23	> **Quick reference** — Layer: Feature · Priority: MVP · Key deps: Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera (designed), Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query (designed in this run), Ship Section & Layout Data Model (designed); Attention, Horror Entities and Perception Filter are designed submitters
24	
25	## Overview
26	
27	**What it is, in one sentence.** 2D Lighting & Occlusion is the presentation-class renderer that turns the simulation's emitter records into the picture: every frame it reads the per-emitter view and the shape table that Emitter State publishes, and draws `Light2D` cones and pools, true occluder shadows, the ring and ship ambient, the material-level hull floor, the emission glow of running machinery and the light textures behind all of them, while owning no simulation fact of its own (no reach, no output, no `lit`, no block, no hook, nothing persisted).
28	
29	**Framing: a data/infrastructure layer with a very large player impact.** The player never meets "a lighting system". They meet a beam that ends hard at the exact place a prompt stops appearing, a wall that throws a shadow shaped like the wall, a lamp that sags when the ship is short of power, a machine glowing in its own colour in an otherwise black hull, and (late) a glow that runs past where their light really ends and leaks the wrong colour at its rim. The system is the *picture of the truth*: the simulation decides what is lit (Emitter State, `lit(ref)`, `illumination`); this GDD decides how that fact is drawn, and the two must agree to the pixel (hard cones at `reach_px` ±1 px, soft pools at the drawn radius `r_off` ±1 px, never smaller than where a prompt can live). The system exists for two reasons that pull in the same direction. First, **Pillar 1**: the physical radius your light actually reveals is one of the few anchors that never shift, and an anchor the player cannot see is not an anchor. Second, **Pillar 4**: a hallucination is frightening only against a picture that has been reliable for hours, and the single place where a light-shaped lie may be drawn is owned here, so that the lie can be bounded, made to leak, and never allowed to touch the real light beneath it. Without this system the game has no honest dark, no readable edge, no lanterns, no tell with a light channel, and no stage for the lie; and the art bible's first spike (the frame budget of six shadow-casting lights, many emissive loops and true occlusion on D3D12) stays unanswered, which the index names as the single decision on which the whole visual direction depends.
30	
31	**What it draws and what it owns.** Lighting is a `PRESENTATION` subscriber (kernel CR-10, KERN:108-113) with one `PROJECTOR`-class sub-duty (the occluder builder; treated as a `PROJECTOR` duty by default, default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), Open Question 5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. It reads last-committed `SIM` views and, for decoys and module-body glows only, `PERCEPTION_OUT` lists; it writes only `CanvasItem`, `Material`, `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D` and `CanvasModulate` properties in layer 0 of the world viewport that the Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera GDD owns. It owns, by name: the light textures; per-shape light configuration conforming to the shape table; the six shadow-casting slots (`SHADOW_SLOTS_MAX`) and their assignment; the non-shadow light budget (`NONSHADOW_LIGHTS_MAX`, of which at most `LANTERN_LIGHTS_MAX` are node lanterns) and its deterministic demotion; occluder attachment over Layout's footprint rectangles (`OCCLUDER_POLYS_VIEW_MAX`, `OCCLUDER_VERTS_MAX`); ambient and the single shared HullSurface material with its floor; emission glow (the unshaded additive emissive layer and `GLOW_HDR_THRESHOLD`); the warm-up, gutter and flicker recipes; the layered **modifier contract** through which Attention's tell, Horror's disturbance and the Perception Filter's decoys reach the picture without ever changing the real reveal radius; the per-light, regional and frame-mean flash governor (`flash_governor`, `FLASH_MAX_PER_S`); behaviour at every rung of the zoom ladder `k_z` in [1, `k_auto` + 2]; and the HR-15 low-vision raise and the reduce-flashing toggle as renderer-side consumers.
32	
33	**Index wording, reconciled.** The systems index (IDX:23, bullet 6, enumeration row 6, Recommended Design Order 9) says Lighting "owns the final Light2D values through a modifier contract: Attention flicker, horror light disturbance and Perception Filter decoys submit layered modifiers; the Filter may add decoy visuals but never changes the real reveal radius". This GDD keeps every clause and sharpens three words. "Final `Light2D` values" means every *value* member of every light (`enabled`, `energy`, `color`, `texture`, `texture_scale`, `offset`, shadow and range members); the local seat's beam *pose* members (`position`, `rotation`) are the Avatar Presenter's (Player Controller PC-5), so the two writers own disjoint member sets (LO-2). "Submit" means *publish state that Lighting reads* (KERN:117: "state that Lighting reads, not calls into Lighting"), never a call. "Attention flicker" is rendered as a **gutter** on fixtures (never the cryo-bay EMERGENCY lamp or the dock glow) and node lanterns only (the verb *flicker* is reserved for deployables, LO-30), an art-bible amendment this GDD requests rather than assumes. "Decoy visuals" are unlit overlays on a Lighting-owned layer and never lights (LO-21), which is what makes "never changes the real reveal radius" structural instead of a policy. The soft-cycle wording at IDX:266 ("Lighting never reads Attention") is superseded accordingly: Lighting reads Attention's published tell tier for the gutter recipe only and never derives reach, output, colour or edge from it.
34	
35	**What it is not.** It is not where light is *decided*: reach, output, `lit`, hysteresis, priority and the caps on emitters are Emitter State's; the Graph's `served_pm` is the only source of a lamp's brightness. It is not a builder: lights come with authored sections and welded modules, and the glowstick is the only player-placed light. It is not a combat system: a beam only reveals. It adds no meter, vignette, fog mask, gamma control or darkness penalty (LO-31). It does not own the viewport, the camera, `RENDER_MODE` or the z-bands (Pipeline), occluder geometry (Layout), hue tokens and hexes (art-director), or which decoy appears and when (Sanity and the Perception Filter).
36	
37	**MVP scope.** Single-player: one seat beam (slots, replication hints and the shape table are sized for four); the home ship and the two handmade derelicts (A with four compartments, B with five); the cryo-bay emergency lamp, which takes the sixth shadow slot; the three vacant beam-seat shadow slots, lent to the nearest wall-near static lights (LO-9, LO-33 mechanism C0) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; one alarm beacon; glowsticks; fault glows for the eight MVP faults that have a glow row; both render passes specified in full with pass A (lights at the 640x360 base resolution) the fallback and default until the lighting spike decides; the modifier contract with stubs for Attention (one tell tier) and Horror; and decoys as a contract plus a stub, because the MVP's single hallucination class (false system state) reaches light only through a lamp housing's own sprite (LO-14, LO-21). Flares, torches and decoy-deployables with their flicker, `GLOW_EXTENSION` and `PHANTOM_SHADOW` decoys, cross-body illumination and the three-ring ambient table are Vertical Slice A; four simultaneous beams and remote beam poses are Vertical Slice B.
38	
39	**Engine posture.** Godot 4.7.2, Forward+ pinned, D3D12 the Windows default since 4.6 (verified from `docs/engine-reference/godot/`, but the installed binary reports `vulkan` in the art bible's class dump, so the driver is written explicitly and printed at spike step 1). The reference folder has no `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D`, `CanvasModulate`, 2D-glow or `SubViewport` 2D-resolution content, and no `scripting.md` or `core.md` exists; every engine statement in this GDD therefore carries a tag, `[REF]` (verified from the reference), `[BIN]` (existence, type or default only, read from the installed 4.7.2 class dump recorded in the art bible 8.4 and 8.10) or `[UNV]` (unverified, settled by a named spike step), and costs the engine reference cannot source are marked NOT SOURCEABLE. The behaviour in this document is written so that a spike outcome selects between stated alternatives and never invalidates a rule.
40	
41	## Player Fantasy
42	
43	**Framing: indirect.** The player experiences this system as the picture itself (what is lit, what is dark, what changed) and never as "lighting". *(creative-director: Framing A "The Honest Dark" adopted as the headline with Framing B "Every Loop a Lantern" as its second beat; Framing C "Cinematic Dread Lighting", lights that flicker, swing and fail for mood and scripted blackouts, rejected because a light that changes without a cause the world can name breaks P1, a scare without a tell breaks P2, scripted events break the "no authored story" anti-pillar, and a liar outside the sanity system destroys the baseline Pillar 4 needs. Logged.)*
44	
45	> The dark here is not a fog. It is a ship with the lights off. The deck plates are there, a step above black, and anything you light shows exactly what it is. Where your beam ends, it ends hard, and a wall throws a shadow that is the shape of the wall.
46	>
47	> Every light you see has a reason. A lamp that sags is a ship short of power. A lamp that dips and comes back is something else, not the power. A machine glowing in its own colour is alive, and you are not the only one who can see it. A red sweep is the ship telling you it is losing. Nothing in the light moves for nothing.
48	>
49	> So you learn to read the ship by its lights, and the dark by its shadows. And when your mind starts to go, the picture is where the lie has to live: a glow that runs past where your light really ends, a shadow with nothing to cast it, a lamp that looks lit over a floor that is not. Every one of them is wrong at the edges, in a colour the sane ship never uses. Trust the floor, not the lamp.
50	
51	**The emotion named: the honest dark.** Trust in what you see, inside a place that frightens you. The horror of this game lives in instruments, sanity and the web; the light is the one thing the player learns to believe, and that trust is what makes Pillar 4 land (art bible Principle 1 rationale: "A hallucinated shadow with no occluder is then frightening *because* occlusion is normally trustworthy"). The power fantasy is **literacy, not dominance**: the player cannot push the dark back, but after an hour they can read a ship from its lights the way a sailor reads a harbour at night: which lamps are sagging (power), which one dipped (something noticed), which machines are lanterns (alive and seen), and whose shadow that is (a real wall, or not). In MDA terms the system serves Discovery (the picture is how a derelict is read) and Challenge (lamp sag and fault glow are diagnostic), and is the main carrier of Sensation (CON:87, "HD pixel art under a light-as-resource rendering model; flow-coded loops glowing in the dark"); it must never buy Sensation at the cost of the first two.
52	
53	**Division of labour with Emitter State's fantasy.** Emitter State owns "the bargain of sight": where the edge is, that the edge equals the prompt, light as a spend, exposure, the reach-for-it falsifier and the per-kind meaning table (EM Player Fantasy). This section does not repeat it. Lighting's fantasy is the **picture**: that the dark is *drawn* honestly (geometry present, hull above black), that every change in a light's look has a cause in the world, the grammar of a dimming lamp, the ship as lanterns, shadow as testimony, how the picture holds at every zoom rung, and where a lie is allowed to live in the picture and how it leaks.
54	
55	**Anchor moment: the cryo-bay wake (the first minute of the game).** You wake. One emergency lamp hangs low and dim in Tungsten (ART 2.2; fixture hex `#FFCC66`), and it **gutters**: a dip of 0.3-0.5 s, then another 10-20 s later, never on a beat. It holds the sixth shadow slot (LO-9), so the pod row throws short, hard shadows down-screen: the room has walls you can trust before you have touched anything. The far wall is suggestion only, an ambient near 3 % over a hull floor that never drops to true black (`HULL_FLOOR_TINT` `#0B1018`, `HULL_FLOOR_GAP_STEPS`). If the pod you came out of carries a light, it is a real FIXTURE placement whose `output_pm` falls in the simulation, never a Lighting-only effect (a Lighting-only glow would be a light that exposes nothing, a P1/P3 lie); Derelict Authoring has answered "no cryo-pod light in the MVP" (DA-23), and any later pod light is a real FIXTURE placement (Ask E-H). You switch on the chest lamp: the light lands on the committed tick and warms over at most `LAMP_WARM_FRAMES` without its edge ever moving. A frost trail crosses the floor in Coolant Ice and catches in your cone. The lesson of minute one: **the lamp you did not choose is a fact; the light you did choose is a decision; neither one lies.** The cryo lamp is also the one fixture the Attention tell never touches (LO-20), so nothing the player sees in this room can be the web leaning in: the gutter here is the room's baseline and the first tell arrives later, on a home-ship lamp, read against it. *What the player must not be able to confuse here:* the gutter (a dip, the lamp's readable radius keeps its size) with a real light going out (simulation state, for example a pod light if the placement carries one).
56	
57	**Second beat: the home ship, conserved (Framing B).** Before a sortie you kill the corridor lamps. Home-ship ambient falls from about 10 % (stable) toward about 2 % (dark) (ART 4.3, `AMBIENT_HOME_STABLE_PM` / `AMBIENT_HOME_DARK_PM`), not because a menu said so but because the fixtures that set it went out. What is left is the scrubber, glowing O2 Cyan `#3FD6E8` along its pipe (an emissive overlay) and casting light at its node (a node lantern), and the reactor cell in Power Amber `#F2C230`: "isolated lanterns in a black hull" (ART 2.4). You can count them. So can the web. The image is the creative core of this system: **the ship drawn only by what you keep alive.**
58	
59	**Third beat: the tell (P2 and P3 in one lamp).** Back on the home ship with lamps on, the scrubber pulls power and the galley lamp **sags**: steadily, and its pool *pulls in* (a fixture served at 600 permille is drawn at 60 % energy with its pool ending at 115 px instead of 126 px, `r_off` 115 px by the integer chain of D.3, while a subject walking in meets its prompt at `r_lit` 108 px, the published `r_lit_px`, `EM D.7`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The junction box at the old edge loses its prompt. A minute later the same lamp **dips**: 0.3-0.5 s at no less than `MOD_FLOOR_PM` of its served brightness, and its readable pool does **not** shrink (no modifier touches the texture radius, LO-18; on a dark floor the soft rim may look a little closer for the length of the dip, which is why the dependable cue is that it returns, Named rule 1). Then again, sooner. Your beam does not change at all (the beam is "a truth anchor", ART 2.7). That is Attention's tell tier, the web leaning in, and the only light-side tell in the MVP's one Attention tier. The player who has learned the grammar knows the second event is not the power.

**LO-20. L2 and L3: the Attention tell is a gutter, the Horror disturbance is a bounded dip (ruled R11; an art-bible amendment owed).** IDX:23 names "Attention flicker" as a modifier submitter and CON:233 names "creaking, flicker, filament movement" as Attention's world channels; an L2 with no submitter in any slice would be dead. The recipe is the cryo-lamp gutter grammar already established as *not a power event* (PIPE PR-13 (a); ART 8.13), applied to **NODE_LANTERN and to FIXTURE of every `subkind` except EMERGENCY and DOCK_STATUS** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)*, with onset spacing shortening by tell tier (tier 1: `G_LO` / `G_HI` placeholder 480-960 frames of `present_time`, i.e. 8-16 s; tier 2, from `tell_elapsed` ≥ `TIER2_TICKS` 600: 300-600 frames, 5-10 s; tier 3, from `TIER3_TICKS` 1200: 180-360 frames, 3-6 s; all owner art-director and technical-artist, routed from Attention OQ-AT-7 / C2; **a tier change caps the pending gap**: the remaining time to the next onset is limited to the new tier's `G_HI` counted from the change (and is never earlier than `G_LO` after the end of the last dip), so a tier-3 tell is not delayed by up to a full tier-1 gap of 16 s. **Aggregate schedule *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*:** the slot stagger (`ONSET_SLOT_FRAMES`, `ONSET_STAGGER_MAX_FRAMES`) is **replaced by the per-lamp phase hash that already exists**: each lamp's onset is its own `gap_k = G_LO + H(id, k) mod (G_HI − G_LO + 1)` frames after its last dip, a pure function of (emitter id, epoch, k), so twelve lamps at tier 3 are spread over a 180-frame span (about 15 frames apart on average) with no slot rule, no overflow case and no collision to resolve; a coincidence that still stacks dips in one region is the governor's to count (D.18), and the tell is a core horror channel that the governor should rarely retime (D.15, AC-LO-77). The slot rule had nothing to add to the hash spread in its own example and left an overflow undefined. A floor-length tell (`TELL_MIN_TICKS` 600) never leaves tier 1, so one lamp can still show zero dips in it; Attention's other channels carry the tell there, Attention AT-9 / C2), carried by layer **M2** (`M2 = 1000 − DIP_DEPTH_PM` during a tell dip; the cryo lamp's baseline gutter is layer M1) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, bounded by `MOD_FLOOR_PM` so it is never confused with starvation: a gutter is an irregular short dip that returns to full and never changes the pool's radius; starvation is a steady proportional dim through `served_pm` that does shrink it ("a dip dims; a sag shrinks"). The beam, beacon, fault glow, glowstick, ambient, reach, temperature and direction are untouched. Lighting reads Attention's published tell tier (an integer keyed on `tell_elapsed`, tier 2 at `TIER2_TICKS`, tier 3 at `TIER3_TICKS`, with window timing in ticks; Attention GDD) and Attention owns the tier's meaning; the filaments that resolve at the cone edge are Attention's presentation, drawn inside the light Lighting draws, and Attention must not count a lamp's light twice (EM-27). The word "flicker" is never used for the tell. **The EMERGENCY exemption (CD-GDD-ALIGN revision; owner technical-artist with the art-director).** The cryo-bay lamp is a FIXTURE but its baseline gutter (L1, 600-1200 frames) overlaps the tell tier's spacing (`G_LO` / `G_HI` 480-960), so on that one lamp an Attention gutter and a baseline gutter could not be told apart and the tell would be unreadable there (P3). The EMERGENCY subkind therefore takes **L1 only**: `M2` = `M3` = 1000 on it (D.13), the exemption set of this rule and of L3 gains it, and no Attention tier ever reaches it. Rejected alternatives: separating the two ranges (the cryo spacing 10-20 s is the locked art-bible grammar, and the tell's 8-16 s is the P2 window), and stating a minimum difference (gaps are hash-irregular, so one observation of a 600-960 frame gap proves nothing). Consequence, stated once: in the cryo bay (and at a dock room's status glow, below) Attention's lamp channel is absent and its other world channels (CON:233: creaking, filament movement) carry any tell there; the lamp still teaches the grammar by its baseline, and the first tell the player meets, on a home-ship lamp, is read against that baseline. Horror's disturbance (L3) on the EMERGENCY lamp is exempt for the same confusion, and Horror confirms it (HE-35: "never the EMERGENCY fixture subkind"): EMERGENCY stays exempt from Horror L3 disturbance, and so is DOCK_STATUS (Horror HE-35 conformed 2026-10-28) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)*. **The DOCK_STATUS exemption (user ruling X2; Attention AT-20 is the authority, CD-GDD-ALIGN) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)*.** The docked pod's dock-room status glow (LO-34) is a self-powered FIXTURE switched by SYSTEM only (Emitter EM-3, E10), `subkind` DOCK_STATUS (Emitter EM-3 owns the token). It takes no L1 gutter (it is steady; the only L1 gutter is EMERGENCY's baseline) and no L2 or L3
**LO-34. The docked pod's status glow is an ordinary lit fixture (X2; user ruling 2026-10-27, Web Map option B).** The dock-room prop of a docked pod carries a small self-powered status glow so that the pod_hop console is always lit; Interaction's refusal of a pod_hop lit exemption (IA-6) stands and the glow is not a fourth `act_gate` exception. *Lighting's side:* the glow is a real FIXTURE placement whose `output_pm` is an Emitter State fact (a self-powered fixture class, Emitter State's amendment of EM-3 and EM-11), so `lit(ref)` at the console is true by simulation and the renderer only draws it (LO-1; P1: never a Lighting-only effect, AC-LO-62 lint). It is drawn by the ordinary soft-pool recipe (LO-7): the drawn edge is `r_off` and the approach prompt sits `band_px` inside it. It is **never rank 1 and never takes slot 6** (rank 1 stays the EMERGENCY cryo-bay lamp alone, LO-9); it is a lend candidate under the ordinary wall-near test, otherwise a non-shadow pool counted in `NONSHADOW_LIGHTS_MAX` and contained by the C3 lint (LO-33) at spill depth 0 (Derelict Authoring places it in every dock room and lints the placement; Boarding BS-19 is owned jointly: Web Map and Emitter State guarantee the glow, Authoring lints the placement). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)* As the FIXTURE `subkind` DOCK_STATUS (Emitter EM-3 owns the token) it is exempt from the Attention tell and the Horror disturbance (AT-20, X2; LO-20): it takes no L1 gutter, L2 or L3, so its drawn energy is `LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM × output_pm` whenever it is on, apart from the warm-up and cut-fade envelopes. **Luminance separation from the visible-unknown lamp** is the art-director's: the glow's peak energy `LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM x output_pm` is set below a fixture's glow and is distinguishable from the visible-unknown lamp's, value [PLACEHOLDER — art-director, confirmed at spike step 8]. | Governor | `flash_governor` (LO-22) | Lighting itself | all transitions of L1-L3, fades, stand-in crossfades, decoy alpha ramps | `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` per light, per region, on the frame mean | never delays a simulation-committed switch (LO-22) |
| (Decoys) | the Filter's decoy list (LO-21) | `PERCEPTION_OUT` | overlays only | `DECOY_OVERLAYS_MAX`, below `GLOW_HDR_THRESHOLD` | not a layer; touches no light |

======
## Acceptance Criteria

Ids `AC-LO-n`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Tags and the evidence each maps to:**

| Tag | Meaning | Definition-of-Done evidence | Where | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `(auto)` | headless, engine-free test against the plan step, with a stub and an injectable clock (the plan/apply seam and the clock are requirements of this GDD, LO-3) | Logic / Integration: automated unit test must pass | `tests/unit/lighting/`, `tests/integration/lighting/` | BLOCKING |
| `(gpu-auto)` | a pixel or counter assertion that needs a renderer; runs in the per-push GPU job, never in headless CI | Integration: automated test on a GPU runner | `tests/integration/lighting/` | BLOCKING |
| `(lint)` | source or data lint in CI | Logic | `tests/unit/lighting/lint/` | BLOCKING |
| `(manual)` | observed in a retained capture with a named signer (art-director, technical-artist or qa-lead) | Visual/Feel or UI: retained screenshot plus sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| `(spike)` | a `(manual)` or `(gpu-auto)` measurement delivered by the Sprint-0 story at the named ART 8.12 step; a result that fails a locked contract is a **failure**, one that moves a placeholder is a logged conflict (LO-32) | Visual/Feel and Config/Data: retained capture, smoke check | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING for locked contracts, ADVISORY for placeholders |

`(review)` is retired: it mapped to no evidence type, and every former `(review)` is now `(manual)` or `(lint)`. **Capture subset:** pixel criteria run on a representative subset of 14 target-rungs instead of all 46: 1080p `k_z` 1, 2, 3, 5; 1440p `k_z` 1, 2, 4, 6; the Deck `k_z` 1, 2, 4; 2160p `k_z` 1, 6, 8, under pass A and pass B; the analytic `(auto)` criteria run at every rung (they are cheap). **Per-push regression set** (no renderer): AC-LO-1 to 6, 9, 10, 12, 13, 16 to 18, 24 to 29, 35, 37 to 40, 41b, 42, 43, 44, 47, 47b, 47c, 48, 62, 67, 69, 72 (lint part), 74 to 79 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (the cheap lints 35, 41b, 42 and 62 joined it; excluded by reason: every `(spike)`, `(manual)` and `(gpu-auto)` criterion needs a renderer or a signer, and AC-LO-70's soak and AC-LO-53's compositions run nightly). **Cryo-bay smoke check** (AC-LO-58 reduced, retained as `production/qa/evidence/smoke-lighting.png`): launch the cryo bay, capture one frame; the emergency lamp is lit, the hull is above black and no DIAGNOSTIC defect is logged. Every zoom-dependent pixel criterion runs on the capture subset under pass A and pass B unless it says otherwise.

### Render contract and isolation

- **AC-LO-1** (lint) GIVEN the source WHEN the member lint runs THEN the Presenter's `Light2D` writes are exactly `position` and `rotation` of the local beam, every other `Light2D` member write, and every `LightOccluder2D.occluder_light_mask` write, is in Lighting's module, the Filter and the tool layer write none and carry no light *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and no real light's `enabled`, `energy`, `color`, `texture_scale`, `offset` or pose has a read path from `PERCEPTION_OUT` (LO-2, LO-25; PC :951, :1062 hold as written); **the last clause is checked by an import-graph assertion (the modules that write light members do not import or reference the `PERCEPTION_OUT` accessor, which GDScript can verify, unlike a data-flow trace) and a runtime meta assertion (a probe `PERCEPTION_OUT` value that differs from the SIM value leaves every light member unchanged)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
- **AC-LO-2** (lint) GIVEN the boot code WHEN linted THEN Lighting registers no state block, no step hook and no `after:` entry, `emitter.state` has no field named `phantom`, `perceived`, `decoy` or `hallucinated`, and the read view's field set at the pinned Emitter State revision is unchanged by per-loop tokens (LO-1, LO-29, EM-29) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
- **AC-LO-62** (lint) GIVEN every light node and every glow that illuminates geometry WHEN traced (**a runtime meta assertion: every pooled light node carries an `emitter_id` meta (and, for the spill node, `shape_id` 11) that resolves to exactly one read-view row of `emitters()`, or, for the spill node, to the one `beam_spill(emitter_id)` record of exactly one BEAM row (at most one spill node per beam), and a scene-tree walk finds no `Light2D` outside the pool** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*) THEN each maps to exactly one read-view row or the one `beam_spill` record of one beam; stand-ins, decoys and the emissive layer light nothing; no Lighting-only light exists, so a cryo-pod glow exists only as a FIXTURE placement whose `output_pm` falls in the simulation, and never takes slot 6 from the EMERGENCY lamp (LO-5, LO-23, CD-R3, Ask E-H).
- **AC-LO-63** (lint) GIVEN every Lighting-owned draw item WHEN its band and mask are read THEN it sits in its PIPE PR-5 band (floor 0, marks +1, Y-sort +10, caps +20, particles +30), carries only the bits LO-24 allocates (1 lit world, 2 unlit overlays, 3 decoys, 4 and up one per live body), and no item is ordered outside the bands (LO-24).
- **AC-LO-3** (auto) GIVEN a stub that rotates the local beam 20 degrees per frame WHEN the frame runs Presenter then Lighting THEN the apex minus the floored chest point is at most 0.01 px every frame; with the order reversed the error is about 12 px and the test fails (D.5, LO-2).
- **AC-LO-4** (auto) GIVEN a fixed tick sequence, camera, settings and a **recorded frame-time trace** WHEN the plan runs live and as a replay THEN the tick-only decisions (active set, slots and lends, demotion order, seat protection, LOD tier T) are identical, and with the same trace every envelope, modifier-chain value, governor outcome and member value is identical too; with a different trace the tick-only decisions still match and the envelope outputs may differ; and an incremental pass equals a full reconcile, including the `ALL` collapse above `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256 (LO-3). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-LO-5** (auto) GIVEN Lighting stubbed out WHEN `state_hash` is computed at every rung THEN it is identical to a run with Lighting active; handlers only mark dirty and all writes occur in the render callback (kernel CR-10, EM-30, AC-86).

### Hard edges and soft pools (mirrors of EM AC-55 / AC-56)

- **AC-LO-6** (auto) GIVEN every HARD row (1-4, 8) and every `reach_px` it can take WHEN the sidecar test runs THEN `|reach_px − edge_radius_texels × texture_scale| ≤ 0.1` base px under both passes (the lint's own tolerance; the ±1 px edge is measured by AC-LO-7), and a sidecar that disagrees with its image fails the build (D.2, LO-15).
- **AC-LO-7** (spike, gpu-auto with retained captures; step 2) GIVEN each beam and the beacon on a flat plane, rotated through eight azimuths (0, 22.5, 45, 67.5, 90, 112.5, 135 and 157.5 degrees) WHEN the edge is measured at the 50 % rim level THEN its position error is at most 1 base px at every azimuth, under both passes, at every rung of the capture subset, including the narrow cone at 1440p `k_z` 6 (1.15x magnified); D.9 budgets 0.692 + 0.1 (pass A narrow, 1-texel pass-A band) and 0.29 (pass B narrow) base px *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, G4; ESTIMATE until spike step 2)*. A failure is a locked-contract failure, not a placeholder revision. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-LO-8** (spike, gpu-auto and manual; step 2) GIVEN a fixture at `output_pm` 1000, 600, 300, 160 and 140 on mid Graphite and on a bright plate WHEN a registered subject is walked **in** (approach) and then **out** (withdrawal) THEN the pool's drawn edge is at `r_off` ±1 px on a bright plate (within about 3 px inside on mid Graphite, ESTIMATE); on withdrawal the HUD prompt persists exactly to the drawn edge (±1 px) and never beyond it; on approach it appears at `r_lit` ±1 px, `band_px` inside the edge, and is never outside the pool; at 140 permille a subject already lit at 15 px keeps its prompt and the pool is 20 px wide; `FIXED`, `FAMILY17` and the raised rim are compared with the art-director present. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-LO-65** (spike, manual with the art-director as signer) GIVEN the hard edge in a greyscale capture at full output on mid Graphite WHEN the art-director reviews it THEN the edge reads with hue removed (ART 4.5); if it does not, the rim step or the curve (`TABLE17`) is raised before the hull floor gap is touched (CD-R4; steps 2, 7).
- **AC-LO-9** (auto) GIVEN `output_pm` 1000, 600, 300, 200, 160, 150, 140, 121 and 120 on R 144 WHEN `soft_pool_scale` runs THEN the published `r_lit_px` is 122, 108, 72, 36, 8, 0, −1, −1, −1 (**sentinel row:** −1 at 140, 121 and 120 is mapped to `r_lit` 0, so `band_px` is 20, 1, 0 and never 21, 2, 1; 150 gives 0, not −1, because `c(0)` = 150 ≥ `LIT_ON_PM`) and `r_lit` is 122, 108, 72, 36, 8, 0, 0, 0, 0; `r_off` 126, 115, 86, 57, 36, 28, 20, 1, 0 (each equal to the published `r_off_px` clamped at 0, and to a brute-force run of the integer chain at `LIT_OFF_PM` used only as the test oracle); `r_draw` 126, 115, 86, 57, 36, 28, 20, 8, 8 (never below `r_off`, hence never below `r_lit`); `band_px` 4, 7, 14, 21, 28, 28, 20, 1, 0 and never above `floor(R × 30 / output_pm) + 2` for `output_pm` above 150 (swept over `R` 24..384 and `output_pm` 151..1000: 0 violations at `+ 2`, 1,392 at `+ 1`); the energy is 0.001 × `output_pm`; and the Debug counters report `r_lit` and `r_off` (D.3). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
- **AC-LO-10** (auto) GIVEN a lamp that commits on at 600 permille WHEN frames 0, 2, 5 are read THEN the radius is 115 px (`r_draw`) from frame 0, `env_warm` is 0, 400, 1000, the light is never enabled before the commit and a switch-off is instant (D.14).
- **AC-LO-11** (auto) GIVEN a glowstick stepping from reach 96 to 24 WHEN each integer step commits THEN the pool is redrawn at the new `r_draw` on that tick with no tween and no flicker (21 px at the last step) (LO-27).
- **AC-LO-66** (auto) GIVEN the beacon between ticks `T` and `T+1` WHEN drawn THEN its axis is the wrap-aware interpolation of `beacon_aim(T)` and `beacon_aim(T+1)` by `tick_alpha`, leads the committed cone by at most 32 units (2.8 degrees), and `lit` is evaluated against the committed cone only; under `PAUSED` the aim holds (LO-27, CP-1).
- **AC-LO-72** (lint and gpu-auto; step 2) GIVEN all five HARD rows WHEN the lateral fit test runs THEN `reach_px × sin(θ_max) + EDGE_TEXELS / D_tex + LIGHT_TEX_MARGIN_PX ≤ quad half-width` for every row under both passes, **and the axial inequality `reach_px + EDGE_TEXELS / D_tex + LIGHT_TEX_MARGIN_PX ≤ A_quad` holds for every row (holds for every row at the shipped default layout: grown squares for narrow, beacon and split, tight boxes for wide and fan, equality within 0.01 base px; the reach-sided art bible square is the lint's negative fixture and FAILS it: 384 + 0.4 + 8 = 392.4 > 384 and 336 + 0.3 + 8 = 344.3 > 336, LO-15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, G3/G4)***, with the lateral margins at the default layout 88.5 ≤ 196.2 (narrow), 140.0 ≤ 196.2 (beacon) and 166.6 ≤ 172.2 (split); and GIVEN a capture of each HARD row on a flat plane WHEN the lateral edge is measured at 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 × `reach_px` THEN it lies within 1 base px of the table half-angle ray (wide 30°, narrow 12°, split lobes at 18.1° ± 10°, fan 60°, beacon 20°; the fan's flanks are not clipped) (LO-6, LO-15). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

### Shadow slots and occluders

- **AC-LO-12** (auto) GIVEN any scene WHEN shadow casters are counted THEN there are at most `SHADOW_SLOTS_MAX` (slots 1-4 seats, 5 beacon, 6 winner); the EMERGENCY lamp at 200 px beats a glowstick at 30 px, a lone glowstick takes the slot, and of two flares at equal `d2` the lower id wins; in the single-player MVP the three nearest wall-near lights hold the lent slots 2-4 and begin releasing them the tick a remote seat binds, completing within 2 × `SHADOW_FADE_FRAMES` (D.4, AC-LO-76) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
- **AC-LO-13** (auto) GIVEN a challenger that out-ranks for 29 ticks then loses rank WHEN 30 ticks pass THEN no swap and the counter is 0; after 30 consecutive ticks the swap starts: the outgoing shadow fades out over `SHADOW_FADE_FRAMES` and then the incoming fades in, and at no frame do more than six lights cast shadows (D.4). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-LO-14** (spike) GIVEN a slot-6 swap on screen WHEN it runs THEN no shadow pops, by the first mechanism in the fallback ladder that passes, or the challenger is demoted after four dwell periods (step 3b).
- **AC-LO-15** (spike) GIVEN the player 10-34 px south of a wall WHEN captured THEN outcome B starts the shadow at the foot like the simulation's segment; for outcome A the band and the engine's behaviour for a light inside a closed occluder are recorded (EM AC-57 mirror; step 3b).
- **AC-LO-16** (auto) GIVEN Layout's `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rectangles WHEN the builder runs THEN the union of the merged polygons equals the union of the rectangles (integer set equality), each polygon has at most `OCCLUDER_VERTS_MAX` vertices, and no actor or horror contributes an occluder (LO-11).
- **AC-LO-17** (auto) GIVEN a `version(section_id)` bump inside a shadow light's reach disc WHEN observed THEN the new polygons are written in the same callback (no frame with a missing wall; no second buffered set exists) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; after a restore `version` is 1 and the rebuild is unconditional, door leaves only after Layout's `post_restore` (LY-12 d, LY-26 c).
- **AC-LO-18** (auto) GIVEN a door of `width_px` 96 and `area` / `area_max` of 0, 1/4, 1 WHEN the occluder is read THEN `leaf_w` is 96, 72, 0 (no rectangle) and no `DOOR_LIGHT_OPEN_PM` threshold is read (LY-9).

494	## Formulas
495	
496	Nineteen formulas, numbered `D.1`-`D.19` in the order of the list that closes Core Rules (LO-32); Core Rules keeps citing them by registry name. Every formula that is not this GDD's is qualified (`EM D.7`, `PIPE D.5`, `kernel D.10`) and is reused by name, never restated with another value. **Integer discipline:** Lighting persists and replicates nothing (LO-29), so floats appear only where a value is handed to the engine in the apply step (`energy`, `texture_scale`, `offset`); every *decision* quantity (counts, ranks, the permille chain, the governor window, hashes, tier boundaries) is an integer, and every decision is a pure function of the committed read view, the committed camera field, the present clock, the per-client settings and the previous decision (LO-3). Every number introduced here is a placeholder, owner technical-artist, "confirmed by the Lighting spike step n"; every `ESTIMATE` is arithmetic on a stated model, not a measurement. Pixel and texel counts are in base px unless a column says screen px.
497	
498	### D.1 Light energy from output
499	
500	The `light_energy_from_pm` formula is defined as:
501	
502	`E_L0 = LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM × KIND_GAIN[kind] × output_pm`
503	
504	**Variables:**
505	
506	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
507	|---|---|---|---|---|
508	| `output_pm` | int | 0..1000 | `emitter.state` read view (SIM) | served brightness; the only source of a real light's brightness (LO-8) |
509	| `LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM` | float | 0.0005..0.0015; placeholder 0.001 | ★ owner technical-artist; spike steps 2, 7, 8 | engine energy per permille; `E_1000` = `LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM` × 1000 |
510	| `KIND_GAIN[kind]` | float | 0.6..1.4; placeholder 1.0 each | Tuning Knobs | per-kind trim so fixtures can sit under beams without touching the shared constant |
511	| `E_L0` | float | 0.30..2.10 at full output (0.0005..0.0015 × 0.6..1.4 × 1000); 0 when `output_pm` is 0 | output | layer-0 energy, the ceiling of every later layer |
512	
513	**Output Range:** 0 to `LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM` × `KIND_GAIN` × 1000 (1.000 at the defaults); non-decreasing in `output_pm`, so **a lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served** (`EM D.1`, Graph D.6). Two bounds on `E_1000`: below, the rim must stay legible on mid Graphite, `E_1000` ≥ lin(floor code + `RIM_VIS_CODES`) / (`EDGE_FLOOR_PM` / 1000 × A_G × c_G) with floor code 1, `RIM_VIS_CODES` 8, A_G 0.0296 (Graphite mid green, linear) and c_G 0.761 (beam green) = 0.00273 / 0.00562 = 0.49 (ESTIMATE); above, the bloom bound of D.8, which includes `KIND_GAIN` and `N_OVERLAP_MAX` and is asserted at startup. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Example:** a fixture at 1000 permille draws 0.001 × 1.0 × 1000 = 1.000; starved to 600 it draws 0.600; at 150 (`LIT_ON_PM`) 0.150, a dim light with a tiny pool (D.3).
514	
515	### D.2 Hard cone scale
516	
517	The `hard_cone_scale` formula is defined as:
518	
519	`texture_scale = reach_px / edge_radius_texels`, with the lint `|reach_px − edge_radius_texels × texture_scale| ≤ 0.1` base px (its own tolerance, separate from the measured ±1 px edge budget of D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
520	
521	**Variables:**
522	
523	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
524	|---|---|---|---|---|
525	| `reach_px` | int | 168 / 288 / 336 / 384 (rows 4 / 1 / 3 / 2 and 8) | `light_shape` REG:121 via the read view (`EM-8`) | the simulation's fade-out radius; for HARD rows it is also the drawn edge; never restated |
526	| `edge_radius_texels` | float | narrow, beacon (grown square): pass B 2004.2, pass A 1002.1 (= reach 384 × `D_tex`); split (grown square): 1998.4 (B) / 999.2 (A); wide (tight box) 1938 (B) / 967 (A); fan (tight box) 1119 (B) / 558 (A) | the texture's measured sidecar (LO-15), produced by a build tool from the imported image | texel distance from the apex to the hard edge along the axis (the grown square: apex at the midpoint of one edge, the reach spans `reach × D_tex` texels of the 2048 / 1024 side and the margin plus band lie beyond the edge; the tight box: LO-15's table) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, G4; ESTIMATE until spike step 2)* |
527	| `texture_scale` | float | 0.1486..0.3832 | output | written to the light |
528	
529	**Output Range:** pass B 0.1486 (wide) to 0.1916 (narrow, beacon; split 0.1681); pass A 0.2978 (wide) to 0.3832 (narrow, beacon; split 0.3363). The sidecar is authoritative; the nominal figures are the layout's arithmetic. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, G4)* **Example:** narrow beam, `reach_px` 384: pass B `texture_scale` = `A` / 2048 = 392.38 / 2048 = 0.19159, so the quad is 2048 × 0.19159 = 392.4 base px square with the apex at its left-middle; `edge_radius_texels` 2004.2 × 0.19159 = 384.0; pass A (`size_limit` 1024) 392.38 / 1024 = 0.38319, 1002.1 × 0.38319 = 384.0. Both draw the edge at 384 (AC-LO-6's tolerance holds: 0.0 within rounding). Wide beam 288 (tight box): 1938 / 288 gives 0.1486 (B), 0.2978 (A); fan 168 (tight box): 0.1502 (B), 0.3009 (A). The cone's half-angle and rim level are baked into the texture from the shape table (LO-6), so narrow (12°) and beacon (20°) share a scale and differ in texture.
530	
531	### D.3 Soft pool scale
532	
533	The `soft_pool_scale` formula is defined as:
534	
535	`r_lit = max(r_lit_px, 0)` and `r_off = max(r_off_px, 0)`, where `r_lit_px` / `r_off_px` are the largest `d` in `0..R` whose integer chain `c(d) = ⌊output_pm × ⌊1000 × (R − d) / R⌋ / 1000⌋` gives `c(d) ≥ LIT_ON_PM` / `c(d) ≥ LIT_OFF_PM` (−1 when `c(0) = output_pm` is below the threshold; `EM D.7`; the closed form `⌊R × (output_pm − threshold) / output_pm⌋` is retired); `r_draw = max(r_off, POOL_RESIDUAL_PX)`; `band_px = r_off − r_lit`; `texture_scale = r_draw / edge_radius_texels` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review)*
536	
537	**Variables:**
538	
539	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
540	|---|---|---|---|---|
541	| `r_lit_px` | int | −1..`R` | read view (EM AC-46b, EM D.7) | the published actionable radius of the integer chain at `LIT_ON_PM`; −1 is a sentinel that Lighting maps to `r_lit` 0, never to a negative scale or band *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
542	| `r_off_px` | int | −1..`R` | read view (EM AC-46b, EM D.7), seventeenth field | the published latch-release radius of the same chain at `LIT_OFF_PM`; −1 maps to 0 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
543	| `R` | int | 72 (fault glow default) / 96 / 120 / 144 / 24 (BEAM_SPILL, row 11) | `light_shape` rows 10 / 6, 9 / 5 / 7; the glowstick's `reach_px` follows `EM D.9` | the simulation's fade-out radius |
544	| `output_pm`, `LIT_ON_PM`, `LIT_OFF_PM` | int | 0..1000, 150 (locked), 120 (locked) | read view; REG `LIT_ON_PM`, `LIT_OFF_PM` (the latch of `EM D.8`, EM-22) | served brightness, the lit-on threshold and the latch-release threshold *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
545	| `POOL_RESIDUAL_PX` | int | 0..16; placeholder 8 | ★ Tuning Knobs | drawn size of a starved light's pool |
546	| `edge_radius_texels` | float | `light_fixture` 1024²: 512; `light_pool` 512²: 256 (nominal) | sidecar | texel radius of the pool disc |
547	
548	**Output Range:** `r_draw` ≥ `r_off` ≥ `r_lit` always, so a prompt can never appear outside the visible pool: a subject already lit keeps its prompt to `r_off` (the drawn edge), and an approaching subject meets its prompt at `r_lit`, `band_px` inside the edge; fixture 8..126 px. The profile is the simulation's own curve truncated at `r_off` (LO-7), so a step of `LIT_OFF_PM / output_pm` of the apex remains at the edge. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Example (fixture, R 144, `light_fixture` `edge_radius_texels` 512):**
549	
550	| `output_pm` | 1000 | 600 | 300 | 200 | 160 | 150 | 140 | 121 | 120 |
551	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
552	| `r_lit_px` (published; −1 is the sentinel) | 122 | 108 | 72 | 36 | 8 | 0 | −1 | −1 | −1 |
553	| `r_lit` = max(`r_lit_px`, 0) (prompt on approach) | 122 | 108 | 72 | 36 | 8 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
554	| `r_off` (prompt kept when already lit) | 126 | 115 | 86 | 57 | 36 | 28 | 20 | 1 | 0 |
555	| `r_draw` (the drawn edge) | 126 | 115 | 86 | 57 | 36 | 28 | 20 | 8 | 8 |
556	| `band_px` | 4 | 7 | 14 | 21 | 28 | 28 | 20 | 1 | 0 |
557	| `texture_scale` | 0.2461 | 0.2246 | 0.1680 | 0.1113 | 0.0703 | 0.0547 | 0.0391 | 0.0156 | 0.0156 |
558	| drawn energy (D.1) | 1.000 | 0.600 | 0.300 | 0.200 | 0.160 | 0.150 | 0.140 | 0.121 | 0.120 |
559	
560	At output 140 the pool is 20 px wide (it was 8 px under the earlier `r_lit` rule while the prompt persisted to 20 px) and at 121 the pool is the 8 px residual while the prompt persists 1 px. Glowstick: steady `reach_px` 96 gives `r_lit` 81 and `r_off` 84; at its last wane step `reach_px` 24 the chain gives `r_lit` 20 and `r_off` 21 (not a closed form), scale 21 / 256 = 0.0820. The 160 column is the case that separated the closed form from the chain: `R` 144 at 160 permille gives `r_lit_px` 8 (the closed form gave 9) and band 28 (it gave 27). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* Baked rim: `FIXED` mode bakes 0.12 of the apex; at 600 permille the simulation's illumination at `r_off` is 120 permille absolute and the drawn rim 72 (0.12 × 600), at the correct radius (ESTIMATE; spike step 2 compares `FAMILY17`). **Spill (BEAM_SPILL, R 24, `output_pm` 600):** `r_lit_px` 18 (c(18) = 600 × 250 / 1000 = 150), `r_off_px` 19 (c(19) = 600 × 208 / 1000 = 124 ≥ 120; c(20) = 600 × 166 / 1000 = 99), `r_draw` = max(19, 8) = 19, `band_px` 1, `texture_scale` = 19 / 256 = 0.0742 (`light_pool`). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
561	
562	### D.4 Shadow slot assignment
563	
564	The `shadow_slot_assign` formula is defined as:
565	
566	`holder6 = argmin over C of (rank(c), d2(c), id(c))` (lexicographic), `d2(c) = (ox_c − cx)² + (oy_c − cy)²`; a challenger replaces the incumbent iff it has out-ranked it on `SLOT_DWELL_FRAMES` consecutive committed ticks; **lent slots:** `lent` = the first `n_lent_cap` members of the wall-near set `W` sorted by `(glowstick first, d2, id)`, a lent incumbent displaced only by a challenger that has out-ranked it for `SLOT_DWELL_FRAMES` and is nearer by `LEND_HYSTERESIS_PX`; `n_shadow = n_beam_seats_bound + n_lent + [BEACON loaded] + [holder6 ≠ ∅] ≤ SHADOW_SLOTS_MAX` with `n_lent ≤ n_lent_cap = min(LEND_SLOTS_MAX, 4 − n_beam_seats_bound) + [no BEACON loaded and LEND_BEACON_SLOT]` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review)*
567	
568	**Variables:**
569	
570	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
571	|---|---|---|---|---|
572	| `C` | set | in-view candidates | read view `kind`, `subkind` | rank 0: DEPLOYABLE other than a glowstick; rank 1: FIXTURE with `subkind` EMERGENCY; rank 2: glowstick, only when no rank 0 or 1 is in view |
573	| `d2` | int | 0..(field diagonal)² | `origin_px` and the local seat's chest point `(cx, cy)` | integer squared distance; no square root |
574	| `id` | int | monotone (EM-28) | read view | tie-break, lower wins |
575	| `SLOT_DWELL_FRAMES` | int, committed ticks | 15..90; placeholder 30 | ★ Tuning Knobs | challenger dwell |
576	| `SHADOW_FADE_FRAMES` | int, `present_time` frames | 6..30; placeholder 18 | ★ Tuning Knobs | shadow-colour fade on a swap |
577	| `SHADOW_SLOTS_MAX` | int | 6 | ★ owner technical-artist, spike step 3 | slots 1-4 beam seats (MVP: one bound, three lent), 5 beacon, 6 above |
578	| `W` | set | in-view non-shadow-kind lights with `output_pm` above 0 | read view and Layout's `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rectangles without the `HULL` flag | wall-near: the light's static `r_draw` disc (the 1000-permille radius of its reach) intersects such a rectangle (LO-9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review)* |
579	| `LEND_HYSTERESIS_PX` | int px | 0..48; placeholder 24 | ★ Tuning Knobs | margin by which a challenger must be nearer than a lent incumbent to displace it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
580	| `LEND_BEACON_SLOT` | bool | true / false; default true | ★ Tuning Knobs | slot 5 is lent while no BEACON is loaded *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
581	| `LEND_SLOTS_MAX` | int | 0..3; placeholder 3 | ★ Tuning Knobs | vacant seat slots lent in the single-player MVP (`SHADOW_LEND_SPARE` true) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
582	
583	**Output Range:** one emitter id or vacant for slot 6 and for each lent slot; slot 5 and bound seats are never re-evaluated. **Example:** the cryo lamp (rank 1, 200 px away, `d2` 40,000) against a glowstick (rank 2, `d2` 900): the lamp holds slot 6 because rank decides before distance. Two flares (ids 14 and 17) both at `d2` 2,500: id 14. A strictly better challenger for 29 ticks that then loses rank resets to 0 and no swap occurs; at tick 30 the swap starts: the outgoing shadow colour fades out over 18 frames and the incoming fades in over the next 18 (sequential, never a seventh light). **Lent example:** seat 1 bound, fixtures id 9, 11, 12, 15 all wall-near at `d2` 400, 900, 900, 1,600: ids 9, 11, 12 hold slots 2-4 (the tie at 900 goes to the lower id), id 15 stays a non-shadow pool under its C3 residual; `n_shadow` = 1 + 3 + 1 (beacon slot) + 1 (the cryo lamp on slot 6) = 6. In a derelict with no BEACON loaded id 15 is lent slot 5 (`n_lent_cap` 4) and `n_shadow` = 1 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 6. A challenger at `d2` 361 (19 px) against the incumbent at `d2` 400 (20 px) out-ranks it but is only 1 px nearer, below `LEND_HYSTERESIS_PX` 24: no swap; one at 14 px against an incumbent at 40 px is 26 px nearer, and after the dwell the sequential swap runs. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review)*
584	
585	### D.5 Beam offset
586	
587	The `beam_offset` formula is defined as:
588	
589	`o = Rot(−θ)·v − a_tex` (`OFFSET_FRAME` = LOCAL); `o = v − Rot(θ)·a_tex` (WORLD); under shadow-origin outcome A the node sits at the chest and `o = −a_tex`
590	
591	**Variables:**
592	
593	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
594	|---|---|---|---|---|
595	| `θ` | float | 0..2π | the rotation the Presenter wrote this frame (raw aim; PC-5) | node rotation, +x toward +y on screen |
596	| `v` | int pair | `|x| ≤ 2`, y −45..−25 | `chest_point` per drawn sheet (5) and animation (REG:521), minus the floored foot | foot-to-chest vector in base px |
597	| `a_tex` | float pair | (−`w_s`/2, 0), `w_s` = axial extent × `texture_scale` ≈ `reach_px` + margin (LO-15's table: narrow, beacon (−196.2, 0), split (−172.2, 0), wide (−148, 0)) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, G4)* | sidecar `apex_offset_texels` × `texture_scale` | apex displacement from the texture centre; **non-zero by default** (apex at an edge, LO-15) |
598	| `o` | float pair | magnitude ≤ |`v`| + `w_s`/2 ≈ 241 (45.04 + 196.19 = 241.2, the narrow cone and the beacon being the largest `w_s`/2) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, G4)* | output | value written to `offset` every render frame |
599	
600	**Output Range:** continuous; the realised apex minus the floored chest point stays ≤ 0.01 px every render frame (lint). **Example:** wide beam, pass B, tight box (`texture_scale` 0.1486, axial extent `w_s` 296.3 with the apex at the back edge, `a_tex` = (−148, 0)), facing south, `v` = (1, −35), `θ` = π/2: `Rot(−π/2)·v` = (−35, −1), so LOCAL `o` = (−35, −1) − (−148, 0) = (113, −1); check `Rot(π/2)·((113, −1) + (−148, 0))` = `Rot(π/2)·(−35, −1)` = (1, −35) = `v`. WORLD `o` = (1, −35) − `Rot(π/2)`(−148, 0) = (1, 113). Aim east (`θ` 0), LOCAL: (149, −35). Outcome A: `o` = (148, 0). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
601	
602	### D.6 Ambient value
603	
604	The `ambient_value` formula is defined as:
605	
606	`ambient_raw = AMBIENT_RING_PM[ring]` (DERELICT); `ambient_raw = AMBIENT_HOME_DARK_PM + ⌊(AMBIENT_HOME_STABLE_PM − AMBIENT_HOME_DARK_PM) × mean_fixture_pm / 1000⌋` (HOME); `ambient_eff' = ambient_eff + clamp(ambient_raw − ambient_eff, −s_amb, +s_amb)` per frame, `s_amb = ⌈(AMBIENT_HOME_STABLE_PM − AMBIENT_HOME_DARK_PM) / AMBIENT_SLEW_FRAMES⌉` (whole permille, at least 1) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
607	
608	**Variables:**
609	
610	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
611	|---|---|---|---|---|
612	| `AMBIENT_RING_PM[1..3]` | int (permille of white) | placeholder 30 / 15 / 5; ordering only | ★ ART 4.3 (outer ~3 % > middle ~1-2 % > inner 0-1 %) | cosmetic floor per ring; ring id is Web Map's (MVP: both handmade derelicts ring 1) |
613	| `AMBIENT_HOME_STABLE_PM`, `_DARK_PM` | int | placeholder 100 / 20 | ★ ART 4.3 (10 % / 2 %) | HOME bounds, independent of ring |
614	| `mean_fixture_pm` | int | 0..1000 | mean `output_pm` of the section's **Graph-served** FIXTURE records, excluding the self-powered `subkind`s (EMERGENCY and the dock status glow, LO-34) (read view; switched-off fixtures count as 0; a section with no such record has `mean_fixture_pm` 0, so the empty mean is dark and never 0/0); no Graph read *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | how lit the home section is |
615	| `AMBIENT_SLEW_FRAMES` | int, `present_time` frames | 5..120; placeholder 30 | Tuning Knobs | slew limit so the frame mean sees a ramp |
616	
617	**Output Range:** 0..100 permille (10 % of white); it never changes `lit` (`AMBIENT_PM` is 0 in the simulation) and is delivered through one setter to carrier B (a material value) or carrier A (`CanvasModulate`, LO-12). **Example:** HOME, all fixtures lit then switched off: raw 100 to 20, `s_amb` = ⌈80 / 30⌉ = 3 permille per frame, so the ambient reaches its dark value in ⌈80 / 3⌉ = 27 frames (0.45 s, never later than `AMBIENT_SLEW_FRAMES`); at `mean_fixture_pm` 500 raw is 20 + 40 = 60, reached from 100 in ⌈40 / 3⌉ = 14 frames. **Self-powered case *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*:** the cryo bay at game start has the EMERGENCY lamp as its only fixture, so `mean_fixture_pm` is 0 and its ambient is `AMBIENT_HOME_DARK_PM` = 20 permille (2 %, against ART 2.2's "~3 %": an art-director point, Open Question 33), never 100; a dock room whose only fixture is the status glow is likewise dark when the ship's fixtures are off. A non-integer step with floor division would take 40 frames and would freeze outright for any `AMBIENT_SLEW_FRAMES` above 80; the ceiling cannot. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A DERELICT section in ring 1 stays at 30.
618	
619	### D.7 Hull floor
620	
621	The `hull_floor` formula is defined as:
622

*Open doors.* Under C0 an open door needs no rule of its own: the leaf rectangle is the occluder (LO-11) and the lent light's pool passes through the aperture exactly as the simulation's segment does. **The rest of this paragraph is the C1 fallback.** While a door is open (`leaf_w` < `width_px`, LY-9) the simulation's segment passes through the gap. Under C1 the door cells themselves (the cells the leaf occupies in the wall line) carry both neighbours' colours like any wall cell, and the one-cell **far-side strip** is its own item whose `light_mask` gains the near side's colour **only while `leaf_w` < `width_px`**, applied in the same apply step as the occluder swap of LO-11, so it follows the committed leaf with at most one tick of lag (the same acceptance as LO-11's door text); while the door is closed the strip carries its own colour only and a closed door leaks nothing. The rest of the through-gap light on the far side is drawn dark. **Named step-4 sub-case, wall-face directionality:** a wall cell lit from a north room shows its lit face to a viewer standing south of it, so the bulkhead can read as lit from the south side; the spike measures whether the wall cell must carry directional (north-face and south-face) items rather than both colours on one item, and until it does the wall-cell lit face is accepted as a bounded sub-case counted by `diag.contain_leak`. That is the sim-lit, render-dark class of LO-7 (a prompt may be actionable in a corridor that looks unlit past the strip), accepted as the lesser lie by the dark-erring rule above, bounded by `diag.contain_dark` (count of in-view subjects that are sim-lit and outside every drawn pool) and measured at step 4. A wider strip (`DOOR_SPILL_CELLS`, proposed 1, range 1-3) re-admits render-lit and sim-dark where the through-gap geometry bends behind a corner, and is taken only if a capture shows the dark sliver is unreadable.

*Stand-ins.* A demoted light's emissive stand-in (LO-23) is **drawn to `r_draw` on every azimuth, with no isotropic or directional wall clamp and no minimum size**, so it ends where the bound light's pool would have ended and where its prompt ends (LO-7, AC-LO-73). Its spill across an `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` wall is the same spill the bound, unlent pool would have had, and it is counted under the same residual bounds: bound (i) for an authored static light (the C3 lint is evaluated at the light's `r_draw`, so a lantern that passes the lint as a pool passes it as a stand-in), bound (ii) for a glowstick, and `diag.contain_leak` for every in-view stand-in disc whose `r_draw` crosses an `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rectangle onto lit floor of another compartment. A wall-mounted fixture, which LO-33 models as touching its own wall face, is therefore drawn in full (the mounting wall is never measured). **The earlier isotropic clamp is withdrawn** (it clamped a stand-in to the nearest `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` edge, drew nothing below 4 px, and made a wall-mounted lantern's stand-in vanish while its pool had been 126 px wide): it contradicted LO-17, LO-23, AC-LO-38/40/60/73 and the zoom-out promise that counting lanterns at `k_z` 1 and walking up to read a prompt agree to 1 base px. The cost it protected was already accepted in bounds (i) to (iv). If a clamp is ever reintroduced it must measure only far-side inter-compartment walls (never the mounting wall), be directional, and clamp up to 4 px rather than omit, and the zoom-out promise must then be struck everywhere and the lantern-count cost put to the user. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*

*Residual bounds under C0 plus C3: PD-1 narrowed, and PD-1b (a scoped MVP exception with a numeric bound, an owner and a closing trigger).* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (i) **Static lights.** Every authored FIXTURE, NODE_LANTERN and FAULT_GLOW placement in the three MVP bodies passes the C3 lint at spill depth `s` = 0, or is moved, or is kept with `s` at most `PD1_EXCEPTION_MAX_PX` (24 px, one wall cell: the user's number, ruling D31, not a placeholder) and logged as a PD-1 exception with its spill depth; a placement above 24 px fails authoring, and authoring may not rely on a lent slot because the lend follows the seat. **Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling R7 (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): the bound stays 24 px and AC-LO-69 stays per-push BLOCKING; no exception list is added for shipped content.** The home ship's `spine_corridor` (144 px between its two interior faces, so `d_face` is 72 px at the centre line, the most any placement can give) is recomputed at the registry's `R_DRAW_MAX_PX` 126: `s` = 126 − 72 − 24 = **30 px**, not Derelict Authoring's 26 px (computed at the stale 122), so it fails the lint as authored and Derelict Authoring must bring it within 24 by the least invasive change (light placement, fixture position or corridor dressing; the room is never resized for the lint). Position cannot do it on this corridor; the lever is `r_draw`, because `s` ≤ 24 needs `r_draw` ≤ 120: an R 144 FIXTURE whose served maximum is at most 754 permille draws `r_off` ≤ 120 (integer chain, D.3; 755 permille gives 121), or hull-side corridor dressing (a placement `base_pm` field and the dressing are Derelict Authoring's levers; a shorter FIXTURE reach would be an Emitter State shape-table and registry change, not a placement, and is not asked here). Derelict Authoring picks the lever and shows the recomputed `s` ≤ 24 (Open Question 31) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R7)* (ii) **Glowsticks, which the player places at run time.** A resting glowstick that is wall-near and among the three nearest wall-near lights is lent a slot and contained; one beyond that set spills at most `r_draw` − `d` − 24, which is at most 60 px beyond a one-cell wall at the steady 84 px and zero once the stick has waned to `r_draw` 24 px or less (21 px at the last step, `EM D.9`), counted by `diag.contain_leak` (in-view non-shadow lights, and demoted lights' stand-in discs, whose `r_draw` disc crosses an `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rectangle onto lit floor of another compartment) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. (iii) **Slot swaps.** During a sequential swap (LO-9) the outgoing and the incoming light are partly unshadowed for at most 2 × `SHADOW_FADE_FRAMES` = 36 frames (0.6 s), counted by `diag.contain_leak`. (iv) **PD-1b, the prop-occluder leak.** The lee of a tall `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` prop inside one compartment is lit by any unlent non-shadow pool; the bound is at most `PD1B_SUBJECTS_MAX` (placeholder 2) registered subjects in view that are sim-dark by a prop occluder and inside a drawn non-shadow pool at once, counted by `diag.contain_leak_prop`; owner technical-artist with Derelict Authoring; closing trigger: spike step 4 reporting whether per-prop render items are affordable, or Layout authoring props that shadow a registered subject's anchor only where a lend candidate stands beside them. These bounds never change `lit`, a registry value or the read view. **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): bounds (i) to (iv) are accepted as scoped MVP exceptions** until VS-B (owner technical-artist, closing trigger spike step 4 or VS-B), with C1 as the closing mechanism and the named fallback (Open Question 21; D31). C1 is therefore not required before lit-item or chunk code. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

*What the rule does not do.* It adds no simulation state, persists nothing, reads only Layout's rectangles (C0 and C3; the compartment-of-cell answer, provisional Ask E-J, is needed only by the C1 fallback), writes no `Light2D` member beyond the existing `range_item_cull_mask` and, for the lend, `shadow_enabled`, `shadow_item_cull_mask` and `shadow_color` (a stand-in is not a `Light2D` and nothing about it is clamped by this rule), and is not a lighting mode the player can see or choose. The decoys' structural isolation (bits 2 and 3, LO-24) is unchanged. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**LO-34. The docked pod's status glow is an ordinary lit fixture (X2; user ruling 2026-10-27, Web Map option B).** The dock-room prop of a docked pod carries a small self-powered status glow so that the pod_hop console is always lit; Interaction's refusal of a pod_hop lit exemption (IA-6) stands and the glow is not a fourth `act_gate` exception. *Lighting's side:* the glow is a real FIXTURE placement whose `output_pm` is an Emitter State fact (a self-powered fixture class, Emitter State's amendment of EM-3 and EM-11), so `lit(ref)` at the console is true by simulation and the renderer only draws it (LO-1; P1: never a Lighting-only effect, AC-LO-62 lint). It is drawn by the ordinary soft-pool recipe (LO-7): the drawn edge is `r_off` and the approach prompt sits `band_px` inside it. It is **never rank 1 and never takes slot 6** (rank 1 stays the EMERGENCY cryo-bay lamp alone, LO-9); it is a lend candidate under the ordinary wall-near test, otherwise a non-shadow pool counted in `NONSHADOW_LIGHTS_MAX` and contained by the C3 lint (LO-33) at spill depth 0 (Derelict Authoring places it in every dock room and lints the placement; Boarding BS-19 is owned jointly: Web Map and Emitter State guarantee the glow, Authoring lints the placement). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)* As the FIXTURE `subkind` DOCK_STATUS (Emitter EM-3 owns the token) it is exempt from the Attention tell and the Horror disturbance (AT-20, X2; LO-20): it takes no L1 gutter, L2 or L3, so its drawn energy is `LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM × output_pm` whenever it is on, apart from the warm-up and cut-fade envelopes. **Luminance separation from the visible-unknown lamp** is the art-director's: the glow's peak energy `LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM x output_pm` is set below a fixture's glow and is distinguishable from the visible-unknown lamp's, value [PLACEHOLDER — art-director, confirmed at spike step 8]. This does not reverse Derelict Authoring's DA-23 (the cryo pod of the home wake carries no light, Open Question 6): the glow is on the docked pod's dock-room prop, a different placement. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

**LO-35. `BEAM_SPILL`, the conditional shape row 11 (D24; user ruling 2026-10-27).** Emitter State registers a conditional `light_shape` row 11, `BEAM_SPILL`: a dim, drawn, honest foot pool of `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` 24 px (range 0 = off, or 24-48; 1-23 forbidden) at `BEAM_SPILL_PM` 600, so an object at the feet in an unlit room does not read as a broken prompt; the row is validated by the dark-at-feet playtest metric, and 24 px does not cover an object one tile to the side. Lighting draws it as one more SOFT pool (the shared 512 pool texture, LO-15; no new texture), edge `r_off_px` 19 px, approach prompt `r_lit_px` 18 px, `band_px` 1, `texture_scale` 19 / 256 = 0.0742 at the defaults (LO-7, D.3) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, a non-shadow light counted in `NONSHADOW_LIGHTS_MAX` per bound seat (1 at the single-player MVP, 4 at VS-B). **Kind, priority and protection point (re-review) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*:** the derived record `beam_spill(beam_id)` carries `kind` BEAM and the owning beam's `priority` (255) (EM-26, Ask E-L accepted 2026-10-28), so Lighting reads kind and priority from the record and never from a Lighting-side table; it is never demoted *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* (LO-23) and its protection point is the seat itself: the foot pool is protected whether or not the local seat's chest is inside it; it may exceed the cap by at most one light per bound seat (1 at the MVP, 4 at VS-B), counted in `diag.cap_exceeded_by_protected`. It is outside the D.19 cut order, except that an `output_pm` 0 spill is unbound like any dead emitter. *Containment (derivation):* the pool is a moving non-shadow light, so beside a one-cell wall it can spill beyond the wall by at most `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX - d` where `d` >= 0 is the foot-to-wall distance; at `d` = 0 that is 24 px, equal to `PD1_EXCEPTION_MAX_PX`, so it sits inside the accepted bound (i) magnitude and is counted by `diag.contain_leak`; worked example: foot 10 px from the wall gives 24 - 10 = 14 px of spill. Spike step 4 confirms it needs no lent slot; if it fails AC-LO-81 the radius, not the bound, is lowered. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*

The section class (`kind` HOME or DERELICT) is a Graph section fact (LSG:174 LS-17); Lighting takes it from Layout's section record only (Layout records it when it builds the section, LY-25), **with no direct Lighting-to-Graph read** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the Graph's Interactions rows do not name Lighting and a direct read would break the bidirectional rule, so the earlier Soft fallback read of the Graph's section record is withdrawn; if Layout ever stopped exposing `kind`, a Graph read would be a new edge needing a Graph row first and is not taken here. **Carrier (orchestrator ruling): the shipped default is carrier B, an `ambient_pm` value read by the HullSurface material per section slot, with `CanvasModulate` left white; carrier A (`CanvasModulate` `[BIN]`, as the art bible 8.4 words it) is a spike-selectable fallback valid only while one section's ambient applies to the whole view.** Two independent reasons: (1) it is `[UNV]` whether `CanvasModulate` multiplies unshaded items too, and if it does a ring floor of 0-3 % would dim the unshaded emissive overlay, the fringe and the beam-edge masks to near-black, destroying "every loop glowing in a black hull"; (2) one `CanvasModulate` carries exactly one value per canvas, but ambient is per section and the home ship and a welded or docked derelict can share one view (3 % against 10 %, wrong by a factor of 3 for one of them). Both carriers sit behind one setter; `AMBIENT_SLOTS_MAX` (placeholder 4: home, one docked body, two spare); items of one section share one material resource. Ambient is cosmetic: it never changes `lit` (`AMBIENT_PM` is 0 in the simulation, `EM D.7`) and can never make an object actionable; it is never a gameplay meter or a penalty. ### Budget, demotion and cross-body light

- **If more than the tier cap of non-shadow lights are in view**: `cut_order` demotes the lowest to stand-ins with `CUT_FADE_FRAMES` fades (D.19); none is dropped and the simulation is never told; a demoted light draws its stand-in disc to `r_draw` (the 8 px residual when `r_off` is 0), the same edge its pool had (LO-23). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **If more than the lantern cap of lanterns are in view**: lanterns are a subset of the non-shadow lights and the lowest-priority ones (60) are demoted first, even when the non-shadow total is under its cap.
- **If the local seat stands inside the drawn pools of more lights than the tier cap leaves room for (seat protection; design review)**: every light whose drawn pool contains the seat stays bound with full shading, at most `LIGHTS_PER_ITEM_MAX` 12 beyond the cap, counted by `diag.cap_exceeded_by_protected`; lights farther from the seat are demoted first (LO-23). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **If a demoted lantern is read at the zoom-out (design review)**: its stand-in disc ends at the same `r_draw` as its pool (115 px for a fixture at 600 permille), so counting lanterns at `k_z` 1 and walking up to read a prompt agree to 1 base px on every azimuth, including beside a wall (AC-LO-73; the LO-33 clamp is withdrawn). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review)*
- **If protected lights fill most of a tier cap (T3 cap 12 with the maximum 10 young fault glows in view)**: the two remaining places go to the highest-priority unprotected lights and every other one is demoted; the floor rule `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` + 2 = 12 is what keeps protected lights from exceeding the cap, and `diag.cap_exceeded_by_protected` counts any excess a later cap change would allow (LO-17, LO-23).
- **If a fifth glowing fault shares a view under `TRAIL_LIGHT_REQUESTS_MAX` 4**: it is still rendered and is demoted only once older than 600 ticks; the authoring lint flags any compartment where more than 4 can share a view; dropping a trail light never drops a stamp (LO-23).
- **If a bound light drops below the cut line and returns within `CUT_HYSTERESIS_FRAMES` (30 committed ticks)**: it is not rebound, so a pool node cannot ping-pong at the boundary.
- **If more than `LIGHTS_PER_ITEM_MAX` (12) lights overlap one tile chunk**: the authoring lint fails; at run time a defect report fires at 14 (`diag.max_item_overlap`); at the engine's 16 `[UNV]` a sim-lit pool would silently vanish over part of the floor, which the 17-light criterion exists to catch.
- **If a demotion stand-in sits beside a decoy**: the stand-in is in its own hue with no violet; the decoy keeps its violet rim on top; both are below 0.9 `GLOW_HDR_THRESHOLD`, and they are told apart by rim colour.
- **If a light belongs to another live body in view**: it is bound, counted against the caps and lights only its own body's items by its mask bit; bodies beyond `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` 4 draw their lights as OTHER_BODY stand-ins outside the budget; a foreign body bit on a light is a lint failure (LO-24).
- **If `MAX_EMITTERS` (96) are all in view**: the stand-in pool is sized `MAX_EMITTERS` − `SHADOW_SLOTS_MAX` = 90 so that every tier, including T3's cap of 12, can demote the rest (orchestrator ruling: the specialist's 66 would run out at T3).
