The chain is `m_mod = clamp(floor(M1 × M2 × M3 / 10^6), MOD_FLOOR_PM, 1000)` evaluated in integer permille and converted to the engine's float `energy` once, in the apply step (an order-independent integer inequality, and the same discipline the simulation uses), with the two transition envelopes (warm-up, cut-fade) multiplying afterwards. **Invariants, each with its own criterion:** (i) drawn energy never exceeds `LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM × output_pm`, and the *steady modulation* (gutter, flicker, L2, L3 combined) never takes it below `MOD_FLOOR_PM` (placeholder 600 permille, range 400-800) of that value while `output_pm` > 0, so a dipping lamp never reads as a brownout tier; the floor does **not** apply to the warm-up and cut-fade envelopes, which are bounded start and stop ramps limited by their own duration and by the governor (orchestrator ruling: as originally worded, the floor contradicted both ramps); (ii) **exempt from L2 and L3: every BEAM (local and remote), the BEACON, every FAULT_GLOW and every DEPLOYABLE (glowsticks)**: beams are the human channel and "a truth anchor" (ART 2.7), beacon and fault glow are consequence-channel witnesses, and the glowstick is locked "steady, never flickers, then waning" by three documents; L2 and L3 apply to NODE_LANTERN and to FIXTURE except `subkind` EMERGENCY and DOCK_STATUS only (LO-20), the dock status glow being a SYSTEM-switched status light and never a tell carrier (X2, Attention AT-20) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)*; (iii) **no layer touches `texture_scale`, `offset`, `range_*`, cone angle, `position`, `rotation` or `color` of a real light**, so the drawn edge stays at `reach_px` ±1 px (HARD) or `r_draw` ±1 px (SOFT) and the hue stays the token's hex at all times; this is what makes "never changes the real reveal radius" structural; (iv) on the same light, L3 outranks L2 (specific over general): while a disturbance is active it replaces the tell dip on that light, then both pass the governor; (v) "submission" is state Lighting reads from the submitter's published view and never a call. Rejected: additive offsets (they can exceed `output_pm`, breaking "a lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served"); last-writer-wins (non-deterministic with two sources).

**LO-19. L1 recipes: warm-up, the gutter, the deployable flicker, fades (`warmup_ramp`, `gutter_recipe`, `flare_flicker`; ruled R12, R20).** *Warm-up:* after `output_pm` becomes non-zero on a committed tick, drawn energy ramps over `LAMP_WARM_FRAMES` (placeholder 5, range 0-5, LO-4's unit) to its L0 value; **the texture radius is `r_draw` (SOFT, LO-7) or `reach_px` (HARD) from the first committed frame**, so the prompt edge and the visible edge agree during the ramp and AC-55/56 hold at rest and during warm-up alike; the light is never drawn before the commit (PC :950: the light itself changes only on committed state). The ramp starts after the simulation's own 0-5-tick arming latency (`EM D.2`), not inside it, so the worst case from command to full light is 10 ticks (167 ms), a ship lamp and not lag; it is linear in energy, hence perceptually front-loaded. A switch-off of a real lamp is instant on the committed tick. *The gutter:* 0.3-0.5 s dips (18-30 frames of `present_time`) no more often than every 10-20 s (600-1200 frames), irregular and never periodic; onset gaps and lengths come from a **pure integer hash of (emitter id, epoch index)**, never the global random generator and never the simulation's `rng_derive` stream (a presentation draw from a sim stream would be a sim-visible side effect; clients may show different gutter timing on the same lamp in co-op, accepted, since the tell tier and not the phase is the information; -> ADR candidate: a PRESENTATION-only stream id needs a kernel ruling); depth `DIP_DEPTH_PM` (placeholder 300, so M = 700 and the dip is 40 % below the floor-bounded value at worst); **the recipe's output `m_gut = 1000 − DIP_DEPTH_PM` enters the chain as `M1` on the EMERGENCY lamp (its baseline) and as `M2` (the Attention tell) on every other fixture and node lantern, and on no other layer (D.13, D.15)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; compliance by construction: the highest gutter flash rate is 0.303 per second at tier 3's `G_LO` 180 (0.121 at tier 1's 480, 0.189 at tier 2's 300, 0.097 for the cryo lamp's 600; `gutter_recipe` measures the gap from the end of one dip to the onset of the next), far under `FLASH_MAX_PER_S`, and the authoring lint is `G_LO` of at least 50 frames (0.83 s). The cryo-bay emergency lamp gutters at 600-1200 frames of `present_time` (10-20 s) as the reference grammar. **Because that spacing overlaps the Attention tell tier's (480-960 frames, 600-960 in common), the EMERGENCY subkind takes no L2 or L3 modulation (LO-20, CD-GDD-ALIGN revision), so a gutter on that lamp is always and only the b

findings.section: Detailed Rules LO-35 containment / Acceptance Criteria AC-LO-81 vs LO-33(i)
findings.finding: Still not fixed. The containment derivation uses 'BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX - d' (24 px, the fade-out radius) and ignores WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH (24). LO-33(i) gives s = max(0, r_draw - d - 24). The drawn spill edge is r_off 19, so beyond a one-cell wall the spill is 0 at every d. AC-LO-81 asserts 'at most 24, 14 and 0 px', which is unreachable and can never fail. The claim that 24 px 'equals PD1_EXCEPTION_MAX_PX' is also misleading.
findings.fix: Rewrite as a derivation from the drawn edge: spill beyond the far face = max(0, 19 - d - 24) = 0 for d >= 0. If the spill radius range 24-48 is ever used, the formula must be rerun.

findings.section: Detailed Rules LO-13 / LO-12 / D.6 (character darkening contract)
findings.finding: Still the top creative gap, and the CD weights it highly.
